overall_assessment: The formal model is clear and internally consistent. The limitation of not handling non-termination is acknowledged and mitigated. The cross-language evaluation is appropriately conservative (NOT_EVALUABLE). No P0 issues.

findings.title: Behavioral equivalence definition does not handle non-termination
findings.detail: The formal model (FORMAL_MODEL.md) defines B(P,I) over all inputs but does not address programs that loop forever or raise exceptions on some inputs. The differential testing oracle in Phase 1 uses a timeout (5s), which could incorrectly label non-terminating programs as 'equivalent' if both timeout.
findings.fix_notes: validator.py handles timeout as GT-T4 (lowest confidence tier). All GT-T4 pairs are excluded from test split. Acknowledged limitation.

findings.title: Cross-language semantic equivalence requires a formal language-neutral semantics
findings.detail: H4 claims language-agnostic representation, but the formal model is Python-specific. A denotational semantics or operational semantics over a shared intermediate language would be needed for rigorous cross-language equivalence claims.
findings.fix_notes: E9 explicitly marks H4 as NOT_EVALUABLE. Phase 5 cross-language uses shared test oracle as ground truth, which is operationally sound.

findings.title: Canonicalization does not normalize algebraic identities
findings.detail: The canonicalization step normalizes names but not semantic identities (e.g., x+1 vs 1+x, a and b vs b and a). These are semantics-preserving rewrites that the current genome treats as distinct.
findings.fix_notes: Known limitation. Would require symbolic simplification.

findings.title: Mutation operators do not cover all semantic mutation classes
findings.detail: Alloy/PBT research identifies ~40+ mutation operators; Phase 1 implements 14. Missing: statement deletion, predicate mutation, absolute value insertion.
findings.fix_notes: 14 mutation operators is a reasonable scope for a first system.
